ety.text: From Middle English idel, ydel, from Old English īdel, from Proto-West Germanic *īdl, from Proto-Germanic *īdlaz. Cognate with Dutch ijdel (“vain, meaningless”), ijl (“rareified, skinny”), iel (“thin, slender”); German Low German iedel (“vain, idle”); German eitel (“vain, conceited”); and possibly Old Norse illr ("bad"; > English ill).
From Middle English idelen, from Old English īdlian, from Proto-West Germanic *īdlēn. Cognate with German eiteln (“to make empty, free up”).
From Middle English idel, ydel, from Old English īdel (“idleness”), from the adjective (see above).

senses.d: Not being used appropriately; not occupied; (of time) with no, no important, or not much activity.
ex: My computer hibernates after it has been idle for 30 minutes.

senses.d: Not engaged in any occupation or employment; unemployed; inactive; doing nothing in particular.
Averse to work, labor or employment; lazy; slothful.
Of no importance; useless; worthless; vain; trifling; thoughtless; silly.
ex: an idle story;  idle talk;  idle rumor;  idle threats;  idle pleasures

senses.d: To spend (time) in idleness; to waste; to consume.
ex: While idling the hours I trace verses / On the inside of wrappers embellishing cans Of Bordeaux mackerel, caught in Monterey.
'If I know William, he'll be settled in some airy corridor, idling the hours until he can ride in comfort.'

senses.d: To lose or spend time doing nothing, or without being employed in business.
ex: to idle in an IRC channel

senses.d: Of an engine: to run at a slow speed, or out of gear; to tick over.
ex: High levels of all pollutants were found during time idling in stations.

senses.d: To cause (an engine) to idle (run at a slow speed, or out of gear).
ex: The driver idled his engine until the car finally stalled.

senses.d: To make (workers, students, etc) idle; to leave without work.
ex: [L]ayoffs idled 1,900 workers in Ohio and 1,000 in Indiana. At the same time, an Indiana assembly plant recalled 1,200 workers.

senses.d: The state of idling, of being idle.
The lowest selectable thrust or power setting of an engine.
ex: A slight valve tap was audible at idle but was not noticeable otherwise.
